note_ja: 戦後、鶴橋駅の周辺では闇市から続く市場と、朝鮮半島にルーツを持つ人々が多く暮らす地域が隣り合い、当時は食肉として流通しにくかった内臓肉を焼いて出す店が集まったとされる。今も駅前で焼肉の店と、精肉や韓国食材の店が軒を接しているという。
note_en: After the war, a market that grew out of the black market sat beside a large community of people with roots on the Korean Peninsula around Tsuruhashi Station, and shops grilling offal, then hard to sell as meat, are said to have gathered here. Yakiniku restaurants still stand shoulder to shoulder with butchers and Korean grocers by the station.

note_ja: 臨海部の京浜工業地帯の工場で働いた朝鮮半島出身の人々とその家族が多く暮らした地域で、戦後、「セメント通り」と呼ばれる通り沿いに焼肉・ホルモンの店が集まったとされる。工場街の働き手の食として、内臓肉を焼く店が根づいたという。
note_en: Many people from the Korean Peninsula and their families settled here while working in the factories of the Keihin industrial belt along the bay, and after the war yakiniku and horumon shops are said to have gathered along a road known as Cement-dori. Grilled offal took root as food for the factory district's workers.
